ns2:section.sectionText: This section will have distributed classroom attendance with supplemental instruction. You will receive an email from the instructor with specific attendance directives. Description: This course surveys social theories from the mid-nineteenth century through the turn into the 21st century, focusing on those that have bearing on conceptions of such important historical objects of analysis as social relations, historical change, the contours of culture, and constructions of categories of race, class, ethnicity, gender, and sexuality. Beginning with "classic" social theorists who addressed characteristics of modern, capitalist societies, the course moves also examines twentieth-century theorists who have addressed how individual and collective meanings contribute to the social distinctions and relations of power, finally, to theorists who have questioned “classic” theories about distinctions and relations from perspectives of new accounts of power and social difference associated with race, gender, the “postmodern,” spatial relations and queer orientations, among others. Two analytical papers on the theories themselves, and one paper assessing the way a historical work applies one or more of these theoretical approaches.
